## A note on story-embedded QA content

Every one of the 26 story files already contains its own `## QA Test Cases` and `## Test Evidence`
sections (populated at story-authoring time, ahead of this plan). This is unusual and a good sign —
it means the automated-test breakdowns below are a **direct transcription and consolidation** of
what's already committed in the story files, cross-checked against each GDD's Formulas/Edge-Cases
sections, not a fresh derivation. Where a story's embedded QA Test Cases and this plan's breakdown
differ in wording, the story file is the source of truth; this plan exists to give the team one
sprint-wide view plus the Definition of Done, smoke scope, and playtest requirements the individual
story files don't carry.

## Automated Tests Required

### Board Renderer

#### BR-001 — Grid↔Screen Transform Pair — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/board-renderer/transform_round_trip_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- Round-trip identity: `screen_to_grid(grid_to_screen(t)) == t` for all 224 tiles on a 14×16 board.
- Boundary determinism: a screen point exactly on a shared diamond edge/vertex resolves to the same
  tile on every call (no NaN, no alternation) — tie always breaks toward the lower-index tile via
  `floori()`.
- Dimension independence: round-trip holds identically for both power-of-two (128×64) and
  non-power-of-two (127×63) tile dimensions.
- Offset symmetry: round-trip holds with a non-zero `origin_offset_px`.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- All four board corners `(0,0)`, `(13,0)`, `(0,15)`, `(13,15)` and the center tile.
- Boundary/tie-break point tested with 100 repeated calls to rule out float jitter.

**Estimated test count**: ~8 unit tests

#### BR-003 — Overlay TileMapLayer API — Integration
**Test file path**: `tests/integration/board-renderer/overlay_api_test.gd`
**What to test** (programmatic cell-data assertions, no rendering needed):
- `set_overlay(tiles, class_id)` populates exactly the given tiles with the corresponding atlas
  entry and no others.
- `clear_overlay()` zeroes all populated cells.
- A second `set_overlay()` call fully replaces the prior overlay (no stale leftover cells,
  no accumulation).
- Empty `Array[Vector2i]` passed to `set_overlay()` clears everything (equivalent to `clear_overlay()`).
- `clear_overlay()` called with no prior `set_overlay()` is a no-op, no error.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Calling `set_overlay()` twice in immediate succession with disjoint tile sets — first set must be
  gone, not unioned.

**Estimated test count**: ~7 integration tests

*Advisory Visual/Feel portion (not part of the blocking integration test): floor/overlay pixel
alignment at 1080p/1440p and the ≤10-draw-call budget for the full 14×16 board — see Manual QA
Checklist.*

#### BR-004 — Occupant-Priority Picking — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/board-renderer/pick_at_occupant_priority_test.gd`
**What to test** (occupant regions injected as `{rect: Rect2, entity_id, tile}` mocks — no live
scene needed):
- Zero occupant regions → `pick_at()` falls back to `{tile: screen_to_grid(p), occupant_entity_id: -1}`.
- A point inside an occupant's `Rect2` that geometrically overlaps an *adjacent* tile's diamond →
  returns that occupant's own tracked tile/id, never the geometrically-underlying empty tile.
- Two overlapping occupant regions with a defined Y-sort front/back order → the front-most
  (closest-to-camera) occupant wins; swapping which is "front" flips the result (proves order is
  respected, not hardcoded).
- `PickResult.occupant_entity_id` is exactly `-1` when no occupant was hit (matches Grid's `-1`
  convention).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A point outside every occupant region and outside `in_bounds` degrades gracefully to
  `screen_to_grid`'s OOB behavior — no crash.

**Estimated test count**: ~8 unit tests

---

#### BR-005 — On-Board Glyph Anchoring Convention — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/board-renderer/glyph_offset_anchor_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- Anchor formula: given a tile and glyph_class with a known offset, the anchor equals exactly
  `grid_to_screen(tile) + GLYPH_OFFSETS[glyph_class]` — no other computation path.
- Data-driven: `GLYPH_OFFSETS` loaded from an external resource; changing a value in the file changes
  the anchor computation with zero code change.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- None beyond the formula itself — this story deliberately has no runtime arbitration logic to
  edge-case (authoring-discipline guarantee, not code).

**Estimated test count**: ~4 unit tests

*Advisory Visual/Feel portion (blocking-adjacent per Test Evidence, but the story types this
Visual/Feel-legibility check as advisory sign-off, not the automated gate): hp-pip-never-occluded at
1080p/1440p with has-acted marker + AP-cost badge co-present; full 12-glyph-class legibility pass —
see Manual QA Checklist.*

### Command & Action Interface

#### CAI-001 — CommandFSM Core — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/command-action-interface/command_fsm_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- `next_state()` exhaustive table test: full 7-state × 11-trigger cross-product matches the GDD
  States table exactly; every trigger from `GAME_OVER` returns `GAME_OVER` (absorbing).
- `menu_model()` AC-1: an owned unit with `reachable()` non-empty and affordable → Move
  `enabled=true`; empty `reachable()` → Move `enabled=false` with the specific reason
  (`NO_AFFORDABLE_MOVES` vs `NO_OPEN_TILES`).
- AC-8: a target both out-of-range and unaffordable → both failure reasons surface on Attack's
  `VerbEntry`; only one conjunct failing → only that reason appears.
- AC-10: a fully-spent entity selected → all AP verbs `enabled=false` + Wait `enabled=true`; a
  producer with `production_cap` exhausted reads "production limit reached this turn."
- AC-2: enemy/neutral entity clicked/hovered → read-only inspection only, never `ENTITY_SELECTED`,
  in any phase.
- AC-3: empty terrain / ESC / a different owned entity clears / clears / switches selection with
  re-filtered menu.
- AC-9: an empty `reachable`/`legal_targets` set → verb disabled with its specific reason, not
  hidden, not an error.
- Pass-Through lint: grep `command_fsm.gd` for owning-system balance-constant names
  (`move_cost|SOFT_MOVE_PENALTY|attack_cost|COVER_DR|CANCEL_REFUND_RATE`) — zero matches.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Every (state, trigger) pair from `GAME_OVER` (absorbing regression).
- Both-conjuncts-fail vs single-conjunct-fail reason surfacing (AC-8).

**Estimated test count**: ~14 unit tests (77-cell table test likely implemented as one parametrized
test plus the itemized AC tests above)

#### CAI-002 — Four-Tier Recompute Discipline — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/command-action-interface/recompute_tiers_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- Tier-1: `reachable()`/`legal_targets()` called exactly once at `PREVIEW_MOVE`/`PREVIEW_ATTACK`
  entry; a board-change (`action_applied`) while the preview is open triggers exactly one additional
  call, never per-hover.
- Tier-2: `Combat.legal_targets_from` called exactly once, batched across the whole reachable
  frontier — not per tile/hover.
- Tier-3: a 10-tile hover sweep across the frontier issues zero additional
  `reachable()`/`legal_targets()` calls after the Tier-1 entry query (spy/counter assertion) — only
  dict reads occur.
- AC-19: a blocker dies to a committed attack mid-preview → re-entering/re-hovering reflects the new
  board state via a fresh Tier-1 re-issue, no reselect trick.
- AC-20/Tier-4: a commit on a tile made illegal since preview entry → `ActionResult.ok == false`,
  0 AP spent, FSM stays in menu with `_reachable` refreshed.
- AC-11: current_ap=9, a reachable tile costing 3 with a legal target in range (attack_cost 2) →
  D-3 marker shown; a reachable tile with no target in range, and an 8-cost tile, do not show it.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Board-change defined against the logical `GameState` model, never scene-tree node presence
  (regression guard against a node-presence-based implementation).

**Estimated test count**: ~9 unit tests

#### CAI-003 — Dependency Consumption Contracts — Integration
**Test file path**: `tests/integration/command-action-interface/dependency_consumption_test.gd`
**What to test** (real Movement/Combat/AP/Base & Production query/commit surfaces, not stubs):
- AC-4: previewed value N for move/attack/build commits → resource (AP or HP) changes by exactly N,
  tested once per action family.
- AC-5: current_ap=9, a move preview costing 6 → `projected_remaining_ap == 3`; a separate attack
  preview costing 2 independently shows 7 (never summed: not `9-6-2=1`).
- AC-6: current_ap=1, attack costing 2 → Attack disabled, reason "insufficient AP (needs 2, have 1)".
- AC-7: `has_attacked=true` → Attack disabled "already attacked," regardless of `current_ap`.
- AC-16 (Logic portion): Build command shows `build_cost`+`build_time` per structure type,
  affordability-gated, placement preview restricted to `legal_build_tiles` with two distinguishable
  exclusion reasons.
- AC-26: a Defensive Structure's attack preview shows/subtracts the queried `DEFENSIVE_ATTACK_COST`
  (1), never the hardcoded `attack_cost` (2).
- AC-21: opponent's turn/resolution phase — clicking/hovering any entity shows inspection only, no
  commit, no `apply_action` call.
- `reachable()`'s in-cap/over-cap render derives strictly from the `is_surcharged` flag, never
  inferred from `min_cost`.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Move preview + independent attack preview shown together — regression guard against AP-cost
  summing across separate previews (AC-5's "never summed" clause).

**Estimated test count**: ~10 integration tests

#### CAI-004 — Cancel-Build Destructive Gesture — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/command-action-interface/cancel_build_gesture_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- AC-18: hold ≥ `cancel_build_hold_ms` → `current_ap` increases by exactly the previewed refund,
  interface returns to ENTITY_SELECTED (refreshed) or IDLE.
- AC-18 negative: a bare single left-click never triggers Cancel Build; a rapid double-click also
  produces no commit.
- Abort: hold released at `cancel_build_hold_ms - 1ms` → aborts, zero refund, zero state change.
- Completed structure selected → no Cancel Build option offered at all.
- Under-construction structure selected → menu offers *only* Cancel Build, refund shown equals
  `BaseProduction.cancel_build`'s preview return exactly (Pass-Through — never re-derived locally).
- The hold is tracked entirely within `ENTITY_SELECTED` — no new top-level FSM state introduced
  (structural regression guard).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Release exactly 1ms before threshold (boundary value — the point of the test).

**Estimated test count**: ~8 unit tests

#### CAI-005 — BoardCursor Input Substrate — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/command-action-interface/board_cursor_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- Bounds: `step()` toward out-of-bounds leaves `grid_pos` unchanged and returns false; repeated
  OOB steps never corrupt `grid_pos`.
- Cycle: `jump_to_next()` over a 5-tile candidate set visits every candidate exactly once in
  ascending tile-index order over 5 calls; the 6th call wraps to the first.
- Empty candidate set → `jump_to_next()` is a no-op, no crash.
- Precedence: a scripted sequence (mouse→A, `ui_up`, mouse→B) leaves `active_locus`/`active_tile`
  reflecting MOUSE→A, BOARD_CURSOR→cursor-pos, MOUSE→B in dispatch order, with zero `Time`/frame-count
  read anywhere in the implementation (grep-checkable).
- Grid-axis mapping: `ui_up` always decreases `grid_pos.y` by 1 regardless of camera/iso orientation
  (never a screen-axis/iso-visual direction).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Every direction from every boundary tile (four corners at minimum).

**Estimated test count**: ~9 unit tests

#### CAI-007 — Commit Dispatch, INPUT_LOCK_MS Debounce & Shared Signal — Integration
**Test file path**: `tests/integration/command-action-interface/commit_dispatch_lock_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- AC-27: two rapid left-clicks on the same legal/affordable option within one frame → exactly one
  `apply_action` call, resource delta applies exactly once, second click inert.
- Lock scope: with `input_locked = true` immediately post-commit, hover/board-cursor movement still
  update live (not blocked by the lock) — the lock gates only new commit dispatch.
- AC-023: `result.ok = true` on `action_applied` → commit-flash begins on the *same frame* the signal
  is received (scripted single-frame assertion, not a tolerance window).
- Audio ownership: an attack commit → `CommandInterface`'s own `AudioStreamPlayer.play()` call count
  is 0 for that event (Combat plays its own cue off the same signal).
- Lock timing: `input_lock_ms = 120` → `input_locked` stays true ≥120ms, releases automatically, no
  manual reset.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Two rapid clicks landing in the *same frame* vs. across a frame boundary (boundary-adjacent, since
  the safety guarantee is structural synchronous dispatch, not the timer itself).

**Estimated test count**: ~7 integration tests

#### CAI-008 — Post-Commit Re-Selection & GAME_OVER Convergence — Integration
**Test file path**: `tests/integration/command-action-interface/post_commit_gameover_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- AC-32: an attacker dies to a Defensive Structure's counterattack on its own committed attack →
  `apply_action` fully resolves (attack, counter, win-check), interface auto-deselects to IDLE with
  no selection referencing the destroyed entity's id.
- AC-33: a Build commit on a legal tile → `ENTITY_SELECTED` holds the newly-placed structure's
  entity id, never the prior selection.
- AC-34: a commit's win-check sets `match_status = GameOver` → FSM becomes `GAME_OVER`; every
  subsequent trigger (select, menu pick, End Turn) is rejected/no-ops.
- AC-35: the non-committing player's instance (inert during opponent's turn) also transitions to
  `GAME_OVER` on the same `action_applied` signal the opponent's commit fires — without ever having
  called `apply_action` itself. Test fixture constructs **two** `CommandInterface`-equivalents over
  one shared `GameState`.
- AC-25: a unit commits a move retaining `current_ap ≥ attack_cost` with a target in range → menu
  re-filters with Attack `enabled=true`.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- The two-instance shared-`GameState` fixture is itself the edge case worth calling out — it's the
  only test in this sprint requiring two FSM instances over one state; confirm the harness supports
  this before assuming it "just works" from single-instance test helpers.

**Estimated test count**: ~7 integration tests

#### HUD-002 — HUDConfig Resource + Cross-Config Loader Guard — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/game-hud/hud_config_guard_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- Violation: `HUDConfig.ap_tick_duration_ms = 200` vs `InputConfig.input_lock_ms = 120` → loader's
  post-load check fires `push_error` AND clamps effective `ap_tick_duration_ms` to 120.
- Defaults: shipped defaults (120/120) → no error/clamp fires, `ap_tick_duration_ms == 120`
  unmodified.
- Release-surviving guard: assert the mechanism is `push_error` + clamp, never a bare `assert()`
  (code-level check — asserts are stripped from release exports).
- All 9 `@export` knobs exist with documented defaults: `pip_max_hp`(10), `action_log_length`(20),
  `ap_fill_flourish_ms`(400), `ap_tick_duration_ms`(120), `turn_banner_duration_ms`(1000),
  `hud_audio_duck_ms`(150), `show_opponent_ap`(true), `show_opponent_fill_flourish`(false),
  `income_breakdown_default_expanded`(false).
- The invariant check lives in the shared loader Autoload, never inside either Resource's own
  `_init()` (structural check).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Exact-equal boundary (120 == 120) — must NOT clamp/error (only `>` triggers the guard).

**Estimated test count**: ~7 unit tests

#### HUD-003 — ApCounterFsm — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/game-hud/ap_counter_fsm_test.gd`
**What to test**:
- `next_state()` exhaustive table test: full 4-state × 6-trigger cross-product matches ADR-0016 §2's
  table exactly; `GAME_OVER` trigger from any state → `COMMITTED` + snap-to-final flag.
- Echo-clear ordering: `PREVIEW_ECHO` active + `TURN_TRANSITION` fires → echo cleared *before* any
  `TURN_START_FILL` evaluation (order asserted via a sequenced call log).
- Opponent restriction: opponent-AP context flag set + `PREVIEW_OPEN` triggered → transition refused
  (stays in current reachable state) since `PREVIEW_ECHO` is unreachable over opponent AP.
- AC-3a: start-of-turn AP reset to income I → committed value equals I, fill-flourish trigger fires
  exactly once.
- AC-4: hover/cancel/illegal-click/no-commit selection → committed value does not animate.
- AC-5a: a commit spending N AP → committed value steps down by exactly N; a second commit's tick
  does not start until the first resolves.
- AC-25: no active preview (including immediately post-cancel/post-commit) → plain committed value,
  no `→`, no leftover projected number.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Serialization invariant: `COMMIT_SPEND` mid-`TICK_DOWN` is asserted as an invariant that cannot
  occur given upstream serialization — the test documents the invariant rather than defensively
  handling it (per the story's own note).

**Estimated test count**: ~11 unit tests (24-cell table test as one parametrized test, plus the
itemized ACs)

## Smoke Test Scope

This is the Sprint 3 critical path — the full playable VS loop this sprint exists to build. Run via
`/smoke-check` before any hand-off to manual QA; a failed smoke check blocks hand-off, no exceptions.

1. Game launches to main menu without crash *(unaffected by this sprint — Foundation-layer check)*.
2. New skirmish can be started — cold boot into the seeded small map (per `scope.md` §5), both sides
   at parity.
3. **Board renders** — floor + overlay + occupant layers all draw at the shipping isometric camera;
   the grid↔screen round-trip identity holds (BR-001); no `local_to_map`/`map_to_local` used anywhere
   (grep check).
4. **Select → preview → commit, for all three in-slice verbs**:
   - Move: select a unit, preview a reachable tile, commit — AP deducts by the previewed amount, unit
     relocates.
   - Attack: select a unit with a target in range, preview, commit — damage applies per Combat's
     resolution, AP deducts by `attack_cost`.
   - Produce: select a producer (HQ or the pre-placed Production Outpost), preview a deploy tile,
     commit — new unit appears, AP deducts by `produce_cost`.
5. **Resolve → win-check → AI reply** — after a commit, the interface re-selects/re-filters correctly
   (CAI-008); the AI takes a full credible turn headlessly when control passes to it (AI-006); a
   destroyed HQ triggers `GAME_OVER` and both `CommandInterface` instances converge on it (CAI-008
   AC-34/35); the victory/defeat overlay appears within one frame (HUD-006).
6. **AP counter and HUD chrome stay live and correct** throughout — AP counter reflects real
   `current_ap`, action log records each committed event, Build button dims/enables correctly
   (HUD-003/004/007).
7. No S1 or S2 regression in existing Foundation/Core systems (Grid & Terrain, Game State & Turn
   Manager, AP Economy, Movement, Combat Resolution, Base & Production tests from Sprints 1–2 still
   pass — this sprint adds a Presentation layer on top of already-Complete, already-tested logic, so
   a regression here would indicate the new Presentation code somehow broke a lower layer, which
   should not be structurally possible given the Pass-Through Invariant, but must still be checked).
8. Performance: no new frame spikes introduced by the board renderer, overlay system, or AI's
   `choose_action`/`AITurnDriver` loop — the ADR-0011 ~3.7ms p95 AI budget and the ADR-0013 ~5–10
   draw-call board budget both still hold at VS scale (14×16 or the actual ~10×10–12×12 VS map,
   whichever ships).
9. Save/load — still deferred (unaffected by this sprint, not in VS scope).

*Smoke tests are run via `/smoke-check` before QA hand-off, referencing this list. Given this
sprint's size (26 stories across 4 systems), consider running `/smoke-check` incrementally as each
system (Board Renderer → CAI → HUD → AI) lands, not only once at the very end — the sprint's own
build sequence (scope.md §9) is BR → CAI → HUD → AI, and each stage unlocks a wider slice of this
checklist.*

## Playtest Requirements

Per `production/vertical-slice/scope.md` §9/§10, these two playtests are the sprint's actual
validation gate — the Vertical Slice's PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL verdict depends on them, not merely on
automated test pass rates.

| Story / Deliverable | Playtest Goal | Min Sessions | Target Player Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Iso-legibility (Pillar 3 hard gate) — fed by BR-002/003/005, HUD-005 | Is the board readable at a glance under the *shipping* isometric camera? Are unit silhouettes distinguishable in grayscale? Is ownership clear by hue? | 1 minimum this sprint (scope §9 floor); prefer a naive/silent-observation tester | New player (cold start, no guidance) |
| Swing-back (tempo fantasy / MVP req #6) — fed by the full CAI+HUD+AI loop | Can a *close, undecided* game be flipped through skilled stabilization, while a *decided* game stays decided? Also capture closeout-drag data (does a losing player spam-produce from the corner HQ and drag the endgame — not a gate, but a flagged observation feeding the base-building/combat closeout GDD). | Sample floor: **≥3 close/undecided AND ≥3 decided games** (scope §9 CD amendment C — exact count at producer discretion within the box, but this floor is the falsifiability requirement, not optional) | Self-test + team rotation acceptable; think-aloud protocol preferred for the onboarding/UI clarity read |

**Sign-off requirement**: Playtest notes must be written to `production/playtests/` (per scope.md
§9's stated location — note this differs from the generic `/qa-plan` skill template's default
`production/session-logs/playtest-[sprint]-[story-slug].md` path; this plan follows the
project-specific `production/playtests/` location scope.md names) and reviewed by qa-lead +
creative-director before the VS build can receive its PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL verdict (S3-11 in
sprint-3.md).

**Capacity note** (carried from sprint-3.md): the full sample floor (≥3+3 games) and the final
REPORT.md verdict are explicitly sanctioned to roll into Sprint 4 if the 26-story build itself
consumes Sprint 3's box. Sprint 3's Definition of Done requires **at minimum one documented playtest
session** (iso-legibility and/or swing-back) logged this sprint — not the full sample floor. Do not
treat "sample floor not yet met" as a Sprint 3 failure; treat "zero playtest sessions logged" as one.

**PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL criteria** (scope.md §10, for reference — not re-litigated here, this plan's
job is test evidence, not the verdict itself):
- A muted/absent swing-back result, or the total lack of the compounding-economy lever, is a
  **PIVOT-to-build-outpost signal, never a KILL signal** (scope.md §7.1, CD amendment A) — do not
  let a flat-swing-back playtest result be miscategorized as a build-quality failure in triage.
- Board unreadable → PIVOT (revise iso art/depth cues or cut depth, re-run legibility playtest).
- A decided game reversing in the swing-back sample → PIVOT (revisit economy tuning) — this is the
  one hard "must not happen" observation in the swing-back set.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified — via automated test result (Logic/Integration, BLOCKING) OR
      documented manual evidence with sign-off (Visual/Feel/UI, ADVISORY per the story-type gate
      table, but still required before a story is called Done — "advisory" affects whether it blocks
      sprint *review*, not whether the story needs the evidence at all)
- [ ] Test file exists at the specified path for all 24 Logic/Integration stories (all except BR-002
      and HUD-005, which are Visual/Feel-primary; HUD-005 still requires its blocking Logic sub-slice
      test)
- [ ] Manual evidence document exists under `production/qa/evidence/` for BR-002, BR-003 (advisory
      portion), BR-005 (advisory portion), CAI-006 (advisory portion), HUD-004 (advisory portion),

## Gaps Flagged (per this plan's instructions — not guessed, surfaced for follow-up)

1. **CAI-006 is conditionally BLOCKED, not just at-risk.** Its own story file states: "this story is
   blocked on the Isometric Board Renderer node... existing as an implemented scene... Confirm it has
   landed at `/story-readiness` time." Since sprint-3.md's build sequence is BR → CAI → HUD → AI, this
   should resolve naturally, but flag it explicitly here since CAI-006's integration test cannot be
   written against a real `BoardRenderer` until BR-001/002/003/004/005 are all merged.

2. **HUD-006 has an unresolved cross-epic dependency.** Its story file flags: "the CAI stories do not
   have a dedicated 'emit selection_changed' story by that name. If absent, this story is blocked
   pending a small CAI-side addendum." This is exactly build-seam (a) named in scope.md §8 — sprint-3.md
   assigns it to "S3-05 Close 3 build-seams," so it has an owner, but the HUD-006 test file cannot be
   completed until that addendum lands. Track this at the CAI↔HUD integration boundary, not just
   within HUD-006's own story.

3. **AI-004's `_score_research_candidates` is a documented, intentional stub** (Research/Tech epic
   not in this slice — per scope.md §3 "research enumeration stays STUBBED"). The story's own AC and
   this plan's test breakdown both call for a test asserting the stub returns zero candidates without
   error, not a test of real research scoring. Do not write a research-scoring test against fabricated
   Research behavior — the GDD's `research_value` formula is fully specified but has no live
   enumeration source this sprint.

4. **HUD-001's AC-1b (render-latency integration test) is explicitly deferred**, blocked on a
   frame-stepped test harness that doesn't yet exist project-wide. This is a testing-infrastructure
   gap, not a story-scope gap — flag it to lead-programmer/technical-director as a candidate for a
   small infra story if frame-latency assertions become needed again (AP-tick/commit-flash timing
   assertions in CAI-007/HUD-003/HUD-004 currently get by with single-frame scripted checks instead;
   confirm those don't silently need the same missing harness).

5. **HUD-006's AC-22 (`MAX_ROUNDS`/`TIEBREAK_METRIC` presentation)** has zero active test coverage
   this sprint by design (`MAX_ROUNDS` is off in the VS per scope.md §5). The story's own text

   than silently omitting it or fabricating a test against a disabled feature.

6. **No story's `Type:` field was missing or required inference** — all 26 stories carry an explicit,
   authoritative `Type:` header, and this plan accepted every one as-is per the collaboration
   protocol's authoritative-Type rule. No gap here; noted for completeness since the request asked

7. **No referenced GDD lacked a Formulas or Edge Cases section** — `command-action-interface.md`,
   `game-hud.md`, and `ai-opponent.md` each have both sections populated (confirmed by direct read of

8. **Board Renderer is ADR-driven with no dedicated GDD** (per the task's own framing) — its stories
